# COMMUNITY ACQUIRED DIARRHEA (NO RECENT TRAVEL)

Consider Clostridioides difficile infection:
[Clostridioides difficile treatment recommendations](clostridiodes-difficile-infection)

---

## Subacute or chronic (>/= 14 days of symptoms)

Primary treatment is hydration and electrolyte replacement. Empiric antimicrobial therapy is not indicated. Investigate for the cause of diarrhea.
Gastroenterology and/or Infectious Diseases involvement is encouraged.

---

References:

- Mandell chapter: Nausea, Vomiting, and Noninflammatory Diarrhea
- Sanford Guide article: Gastroenteritis, Diarrhea: Overview
- DOI: 10.1093/cid/cix669-Shane et al, Clinical Infectious Diseases 2017,
- 65(12):45-80
- Up-To-Date article: Approach to the adult with acute diarrhea in resource-rich settings
Therapy:
## Primary treatment

Hydration and electrolyte replacement

## Empiric antimicrobial treatment

Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h for 3-5 days [R,DI]
Alternative
Azithromycin 1000 mg PO one-time dose [M]
< OR >
Azithromycin 500 mg PO q24h for 3 days [M]
Outpt: ORZID3 GMENU COM ACQ DIARRHEA/NO TRAVEL
